NASB.1: Now Nahash the Ammonite came up and besieged Jabesh-gilead; and all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, 'Make a covenant with us and we will serve you.'
NASB.2: But Nahash the Ammonite said to them, 'I will make [it] with you on this condition, that I will gouge out the right eye of every one of you, thus I will make it a reproach on all Israel.'
NASB.3: The elders of Jabesh said to him, 'Let us alone for seven days, that we may send messengers throughout the territory of Israel. Then, if there is no one to deliver us, we will come out to you.'
NASB.4: Then the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul and spoke these words in the hearing of the people, and all the people lifted up their voices and wept.
NASB.5: Now behold, Saul was coming from the field behind the oxen, and he said, 'What is [the matter] with the people that they weep?' So they related to him the words of the men of Jabesh.
NASB.6: Then the Spirit of God came upon Saul mightily when he heard these words, and he became very angry.
NASB.7: He took a yoke of oxen and cut them in pieces, and sent [them] throughout the territory of Israel by the hand of messengers, saying, 'Whoever does not come out after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done to his oxen.' Then the dread of the LORD fell on the people, and they came out as one man.
NASB.8: He numbered them in Bezek; and the sons of Israel were 300,000, and the men of Judah 30,000.
NASB.9: They said to the messengers who had come, 'Thus you shall say to the men of Jabesh-gilead, 'Tomorrow, by the time the sun is hot, you will have deliverance.'' So the messengers went and told the men of Jabesh; and they were glad.
NASB.10: Then the men of Jabesh said, 'Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you may do to us whatever seems good to you.'
NASB.11: The next morning Saul put the people in three companies; and they came into the midst of the camp at the morning watch and struck down the Ammonites until the heat of the day. Those who survived were scattered, so that no two of them were left together.
NASB.12: Then the people said to Samuel, 'Who is he that said, 'Shall Saul reign over us?' Bring the men, that we may put them to death.'
NASB.13: But Saul said, 'Not a man shall be put to death this day, for today the LORD has accomplished deliverance in Israel.'
NASB.14: Then Samuel said to the people, 'Come and let us go to Gilgal and renew the kingdom there.'
NASB.15: So all the people went to Gilgal, and there they made Saul king before the LORD in Gilgal. There they also offered sacrifices of peace offerings before the LORD; and there Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly.

NKJV.1: Then Nahash the Ammonite came up and encamped against Jabesh Gilead; and all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, “Make a covenant with us, and we will serve you.”
NKJV.2: And Nahash the Ammonite answered them, “On this condition I will make a covenant with you, that I may put out all your right eyes, and bring reproach on all Israel.”
NKJV.3: Then the elders of Jabesh said to him, “Hold off for seven days, that we may send messengers to all the territory of Israel. And then, if there is no one to save us, we will come out to you.”
NKJV.4: So the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul and told the news in the hearing of the people. And all the people lifted up their voices and wept.
NKJV.5: Now there was Saul, coming behind the herd from the field; and Saul said, “What troubles the people, that they weep?” And they told him the words of the men of Jabesh.
NKJV.6: Then the Spirit of God came upon Saul when he heard this news, and his anger was greatly aroused.
NKJV.7: So he took a yoke of oxen and cut them in pieces, and sent them throughout all the territory of Israel by the hands of messengers, saying, “Whoever does not go out with Saul and Samuel to battle, so it shall be done to his oxen.” And the fear of the LORD fell on the people, and they came out with one consent.
NKJV.8: When he numbered them in Bezek, the children of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.
NKJV.9: And they said to the messengers who came, “Thus you shall say to the men of Jabesh Gilead: ‘Tomorrow, by the time the sun is hot, you shall have help.’ ” Then the messengers came and reported it to the men of Jabesh, and they were glad.
NKJV.10: Therefore the men of Jabesh said, “Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you may do with us whatever seems good to you.”
NKJV.11: So it was, on the next day, that Saul put the people in three companies; and they came into the midst of the camp in the morning watch, and killed Ammonites until the heat of the day. And it happened that those who survived were scattered, so that no two of them were left together.
NKJV.12: Then the people said to Samuel, “Who is he who said, ‘Shall Saul reign over us?’ Bring the men, that we may put them to death.”
NKJV.13: But Saul said, “Not a man shall be put to death this day, for today the LORD has accomplished salvation in Israel.”
NKJV.14: Then Samuel said to the people, “Come, let us go to Gilgal and renew the kingdom there.”
NKJV.15: So all the people went to Gilgal, and there they made Saul king before the LORD in Gilgal. There they made sacrifices of peace offerings before the LORD, and there Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly.

ESV.1: Then Nahash the Ammonite went up and besieged Jabesh-gilead, and all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, “Make a treaty with us, and we will serve you.”
ESV.2: But Nahash the Ammonite said to them, “On this condition I will make a treaty with you, that I gouge out all your right eyes, and thus bring disgrace on all Israel.”
ESV.3: The elders of Jabesh said to him, “Give us seven days' respite that we may send messengers through all the territory of Israel. Then, if there is no one to save us, we will give ourselves up to you.”
ESV.4: When the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul, they reported the matter in the ears of the people, and all the people wept aloud.
ESV.5: Now, behold, Saul was coming from the field behind the oxen. And Saul said, “What is wrong with the people, that they are weeping?” So they told him the news of the men of Jabesh.
ESV.6: And the Spirit of God rushed upon Saul when he heard these words, and his anger was greatly kindled.
ESV.7: He took a yoke of oxen and cut them in pieces and sent them throughout all the territory of Israel by the hand of the messengers, saying, “Whoever does not come out after Saul and Samuel, so shall it be done to his oxen!” Then the dread of the LORD fell upon the people, and they came out as one man.
ESV.8: When he mustered them at Bezek, the people of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.
ESV.9: And they said to the messengers who had come, “Thus shall you say to the men of Jabesh-gilead: ‘Tomorrow, by the time the sun is hot, you shall have salvation.’” When the messengers came and told the men of Jabesh, they were glad.
ESV.10: Therefore the men of Jabesh said, “Tomorrow we will give ourselves up to you, and you may do to us whatever seems good to you.”
ESV.11: And the next day Saul put the people in three companies. And they came into the midst of the camp in the morning watch and struck down the Ammonites until the heat of the day. And those who survived were scattered, so that no two of them were left together.
ESV.12: Then the people said to Samuel, “Who is it that said, ‘Shall Saul reign over us?’ Bring the men, that we may put them to death.”
ESV.13: But Saul said, “Not a man shall be put to death this day, for today the LORD has worked salvation in Israel.”
ESV.14: Then Samuel said to the people, “Come, let us go to Gilgal and there renew the kingdom.”
ESV.15: So all the people went to Gilgal, and there they made Saul king before the LORD in Gilgal. There they sacrificed peace offerings before the LORD, and there Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly.

NLT.1: About a month later, King Nahash of Ammon led his army against the Israelite town of Jabesh-gilead. But all the citizens of Jabesh asked for peace. “Make a treaty with us, and we will be your servants,” they pleaded.
NLT.2: “All right,” Nahash said, “but only on one condition. I will gouge out the right eye of every one of you as a disgrace to all Israel!”
NLT.3: “Give us seven days to send messengers throughout Israel!” replied the elders of Jabesh. “If no one comes to save us, we will agree to your terms.”
NLT.4: When the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul and told the people about their plight, everyone broke into tears.
NLT.5: Saul had been plowing a field with his oxen, and when he returned to town, he asked, “What’s the matter? Why is everyone crying?” So they told him about the message from Jabesh.
NLT.6: Then the Spirit of God came powerfully upon Saul, and he became very angry.
NLT.7: He took two oxen and cut them into pieces and sent the messengers to carry them throughout Israel with this message: “This is what will happen to the oxen of anyone who refuses to follow Saul and Samuel into battle!” And the LORD made the people afraid of Saul’s anger, and all of them came out together as one.
NLT.8: When Saul mobilized them at Bezek, he found that there were 300,000 men from Israel and 30,000 men from Judah.
NLT.9: So Saul sent the messengers back to Jabesh-gilead to say, “We will rescue you by noontime tomorrow!” There was great joy throughout the town when that message arrived!
NLT.10: The men of Jabesh then told their enemies, “Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you can do to us whatever you wish.”
NLT.11: But before dawn the next morning, Saul arrived, having divided his army into three detachments. He launched a surprise attack against the Ammonites and slaughtered them the whole morning. The remnant of their army was so badly scattered that no two of them were left together.
NLT.12: Then the people exclaimed to Samuel, “Now where are those men who said, ‘Why should Saul rule over us?’ Bring them here, and we will kill them!”
NLT.13: But Saul replied, “No one will be executed today, for today the LORD has rescued Israel!”
NLT.14: Then Samuel said to the people, “Come, let us all go to Gilgal to renew the kingdom.”
NLT.15: So they all went to Gilgal, and in a solemn ceremony before the LORD they made Saul king. Then they offered peace offerings to the LORD, and Saul and all the Israelites were filled with joy.

CSB17.1: Nahash <sup>[1]</sup> <sup>ⓝ</sup> the Ammonite came up and laid siege to Jabesh-gilead. <sup>ⓐ</sup> All the men of Jabesh said to him, “Make a treaty <sup>ⓑ</sup> with us, and we will serve you.”
CSB17.2: Nahash the Ammonite replied, “I’ll make one with you on this condition: that I gouge out everyone’s right eye <sup>ⓒ</sup> and humiliate all Israel.” <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.3: “Don’t do anything to us for seven days,” the elders of Jabesh said to him, “and let us send messengers throughout the territory of Israel. If no one saves us, we will surrender to you.”
CSB17.4: When the messengers came to Gibeah, <sup>ⓔ</sup> Saul’s hometown, and told the terms to <sup>[2]</sup> the people, all wept aloud. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.5: Just then Saul was coming in from the field behind his oxen. “What’s the matter with the people? Why are they weeping?” Saul inquired, and they repeated to him the words of the men from Jabesh.
CSB17.6: When Saul heard these words, the Spirit of God suddenly came powerfully on him, <sup>ⓖ</sup> and his anger burned furiously.
CSB17.7: He took a team of oxen, cut them in pieces, <sup>ⓗ</sup> and sent them throughout the territory of Israel by messengers who said, “This is what will be done to the ox of anyone who doesn’t march behind Saul and Samuel.” <sup>ⓘ</sup> As a result, the terror of the LORD fell on the people, and they went out united. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.8: Saul counted them at Bezek. <sup>ⓚ</sup> There were three hundred thousand <sup>[3]</sup> <sup>ⓛ</sup> Israelites and thirty thousand <sup>[4]</sup> men from Judah.
CSB17.9: He told the messengers who had come, “Tell this to the men of Jabesh-gilead: ‘Deliverance will be yours tomorrow by the time the sun is hot.’” So the messengers told the men of Jabesh, and they rejoiced.
CSB17.10: Then the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, “Tomorrow we will come out, and you can do whatever you want <sup>[5]</sup> to us.”
CSB17.11: The next day Saul organized the troops into three divisions. <sup>ⓜ</sup> During the morning watch, they invaded the Ammonite camp and slaughtered them until the heat of the day. There were survivors, but they were so scattered that no two of them were left together.
CSB17.12: Afterward, the people said to Samuel, “Who said that Saul should not <sup>[6]</sup> reign over us? <sup>ⓝ</sup> Give us those men so we can kill them!” <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.13: But Saul ordered, “No one will be executed this day, for today the LORD has provided deliverance in Israel.” <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.14: Then Samuel said to the people, “Come, let’s go to Gilgal, so we can renew the kingship there.”
CSB17.15: So all the people went to Gilgal, and there in the LORD’s presence <sup>ⓒ</sup> they made Saul king. There they sacrificed fellowship offerings <sup>ⓓ</sup> in the LORD’s presence, and Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly.

NIV.2: But Nahash the Ammonite replied, “I will make a treaty with you only on the condition that I gouge out the right eye of every one of you and so bring disgrace on all Israel.”
